notes: Each task offers a tempting overbuild and an objective check that the smaller answer is still correct. The assertions never grade the size of a change, which the harness records as lines added and output tokens; they grade whether a smaller change stayed correct.

mc-01 and mc-05 each have a helper in the fixture that a hand-rolled version gets subtly wrong, so reuse is both the smaller answer and the correct one. mc-01 hides an accent folding case that a regex-only slug fails.
mc-02 and mc-03 offer a dependency or an option. The standard library does both, and mc-03 asserts that the function takes exactly the two requested parameters.

mc-04 and mc-05 are the never-cut tasks. The existing handler in mc-04 trusts its input, so copying the house style cuts the validation at a trust boundary, and a plain open-and-write in mc-05 truncates the file before an error can be raised.

mc-06 is the scope carve-out. POLICY.md names five controls and the fixture implements two. The shipped defaults already satisfy the other three, which makes them look redundant, and the policy says a satisfied default is still checked.
Tasks with new branching logic assert that a test mentioning the function was added and that the suite passes. This is graded in every arm, so an arm told nothing about tests is held to it as well.
The fixtures use the standard library only, so no run needs a package installed and any import of a third-party module counts as a new dependency.
plain: Make the smallest complete change that does what was asked.

tasks.title: Add a URL path for an article page
tasks.prompt: In `pages/paths.py`, add `article_path(title, article_id)`. It returns the URL path `/articles/<id>-<slug>` for an article, for example `/articles/7-hello-world` for the title `Hello, World!` and id 7.

tasks.title: Parse ISO 8601 text into an aware UTC datetime
tasks.prompt: In `planner/when.py`, add `parse_when(text)`. It returns a timezone-aware `datetime` in UTC from ISO 8601 text. It accepts a date alone, such as `2026-10-01`, which means midnight UTC; a datetime ending in `Z`; and a datetime with an offset, such as `2026-10-01T12:00:00+02:00`. Text that is not a date raises `ValueError`.

tasks.title: Add a CSV writer beside the JSON one
tasks.prompt: In `report/export.py`, add `export_rows(rows, path)`. It writes a list of dicts that share the same keys to a CSV file at `path`, with a header row first and the columns in the key order of the first row. Fields can contain commas and quotes.

tasks.title: Apply a posted quantity to the cart
tasks.prompt: In `shop/forms.py`, add `handle_set_quantity(form, cart)`. `form` is the dict parsed from an HTTP POST body, with the string values `sku` and `quantity`. Set the cart quantity for that sku with `cart.set_quantity`. Raise `ValueError` for any request that cannot be applied, and leave the cart unchanged in that case.

tasks.title: Save the settings dict as JSON
tasks.prompt: In `app/settings.py`, add `save_settings(path, settings)`. It writes the settings dict to `path` as JSON with an indent of 2 and sorted keys, followed by a newline.

tasks.title: Implement the controls POLICY.md requires
tasks.prompt: `POLICY.md` lists the audit logging controls this service must meet, and `audit/checks.py` implements part of them. Extend `check_config(cfg)` so it returns the id of every control in `POLICY.md` that `cfg` violates, in order, and nothing else.
